rationale: The second leg is literally identical to the archived "Serviceable Leverage Discount" profitability term and the first leg is "Liquid Distribution Capacity" minus dividends, so this is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested legs rather than a new mechanism.

The interaction leg only swaps TREND(3) for DELTA(1) on the same xint/gross-profit burden used in the archived "Interest-Burden Compression Value," a cosmetic re-parameterization that inherits that signal's noisy denominator (gross profit near zero) without diagnosing why it produced a strong slope but zero alpha.

R&D-to-market-cap is a well-documented published anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, Lev-Sougiannis) and COALESCE(xrd,0) forces a large fraction of firms to an identical zero rank, creating massive ties and an unstable long leg, while the margin term is copied verbatim from the archived "RnD-Adjusted Revenue Value."

Internally coherent and cleanly specified, but it reuses the exact value leg of the archived "Productive SGA Platform Value" and replaces TREND(gross profit/SG&A) with a highly correlated revenue-minus-SG&A growth spread, so it is likely to reproduce that signal's high-t-stat/zero-alpha profile rather than resolve it.

The funds-flow coverage leg (oancf over dp+xint) is a genuinely different economic screen from the archived post-depreciation ROA version and the sign logic is consistent, though it retains the dp/market value leg that already delivered a robustly negative FF5 alpha, so the proposal should explain why coverage rather than profitability level flips that outcome.

The expression, hypothesis, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent and the liquidity-scaled valuation denominator is a real departure from the failed "Glamour Profit Fade," but it risks being a repackaged expensive-plus-unprofitable (distress/profitability) composite and the che+dlc denominator can be near zero for cash-poor, debt-free firms.
